source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — press releases on sovereign rating actions
why_relevant: Sovereign rating actions (Fitch A-, S&P A, Moody's A3) cap or anchor SK bank ratings; the ministry's Slovak-language releases are a fast, free notification channel for the sovereign leg of bank rating changes.

source_name: Slovak business media rating coverage (SITA, Pravda Ekonomika, Forbes SK, SME Index)
why_relevant: Slovak-language reporting on rating-agency actions and bank ratings, often quoting rationale from otherwise paywalled agency releases; SITA maintains a Fitch Ratings tag page usable as a low-cost SK feed.

source_name: IDEAS/RePEc — IMF Slovak Republic country report index
why_relevant: Stable bibliographic index of IMF SVK country reports (including FSAP notes) with persistent handles — resilient discovery layer when imf.org page structures change.

source_name: SZRB – Tlačové správy (press release archive)
why_relevant: Press-release archive announcing results, new products, guarantee schemes and consolidated performance with subsidiary SIH; earliest public signal of strategy and programme launches.

source_name: EXIMBANKA SR – Výročné správy (annual reports index, sk/en bilingual)
why_relevant: Export-Import Bank of the Slovak Republic publishes a long, bilingual back-catalogue of annual reports (observed links back to 2006) plus supplements; covers both banking and export-credit insurance activity of a state institution.

source_name: EXIMBANKA SR – news / results announcements
why_relevant: Interim and full-year performance announcements (banking vs insurance split, supported export volumes) ahead of the formal annual report.

source_name: Slovak Investment Holding, a. s. – Dokumenty (annual reports)
why_relevant: SIH (historically SZRB Asset Management) is the state fund-of-funds / development finance vehicle now consolidated into SZRB; its document page carries annual reports and fund documentation relevant to public-money financing flows.

source_name: MF SR – Špecializované inštitúcie finančného trhu: SZRB
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance owner-page for SZRB: legal basis, mandate, shareholder-rights framing, and links onward to bank disclosures — a stable pointer that survives bank website redesigns.

source_name: MF SR – Exportno-importná banka SR (institution page)
why_relevant: Ministry-side page for EXIMBANKA SR; documents statutory reporting duties and governance, useful to time when annual reports must appear.

source_name: MF SR – Súhrnná výročná správa SR (consolidated annual report of the Slovak Republic)
why_relevant: Statutory consolidated annual report of the whole Slovak state (per Act 523/2004 Z. z.), consolidating state-owned financial entities; gives comparable multi-year figures and the official list of consolidated units.

source_name: Slovenská konsolidačná, a. s. – výročné správy
why_relevant: 100% MF SR-owned state receivables consolidation company (Act 374/2014 Z. z.); annual reports reveal state debt-collection volumes, IT/service procurement and public-sector receivable flows.

source_name: MF SR – organizácie s účasťou štátu / výkon akcionárskych práv
why_relevant: Ministry index of entities where MF SR exercises shareholder rights — the authoritative actor map for the state-owned financial perimeter in Slovakia; snowball seed for further entities.

source_name: rokovania.gov.sk – Portál právnych predpisov / government session materials
why_relevant: Government session portal where statutory sector reports are tabled (e.g. NBS Správa o finančnej stabilite, Správa o stave a vývoji finančného trhu) together with cover notes, ministry comments and annexes not published elsewhere.

source_name: hsr.rokovania.sk / lrv.rokovania.sk – tripartite and Legislative Council document archives
why_relevant: Sub-portals of the government document system holding older sector reports and attachments (e.g. Správa o stave a vývoji finančného trhu 2009; a Slovenská konsolidačná item on lrv). Useful for historical depth where the main portal has purged items.

source_name: NBS – Správa o stave a vývoji finančného trhu (Financial Market Situation and Trend Report)
why_relevant: The statutory sector report NBS submits to the government/parliament; the aggregate benchmark against which individual state-bank disclosures are read. Bilingual (sk landing exists too).

source_name: NKÚ SR – Najvyšší kontrolný úrad, control findings on state financial institutions
why_relevant: Supreme Audit Office audits of SZRB and EXIMBANKA (e.g. risky-receivables audit covering 2019-2021, published Dec 2022) expose internal process, IT/system and governance detail that annual reports omit; searchable findings and controllable-subject databases.

source_name: NR SR – parlamentné tlače / materiály doručené NR SR
why_relevant: Parliamentary reporting duty channel: annual reports and sector reports of state institutions and audit bodies arrive here as numbered prints with committee handling; often the only public copy of an annex.

source_name: Centrálny register zmlúv (CRZ) – contracts of state financial entities
why_relevant: Mandatory publication of all contracts of state entities; reveals vendors, IT/payments suppliers, values and durations behind SZRB/SIH/EXIMBANKA/Slovenská konsolidačná — competitive intelligence that never appears in an annual report.

source_name: Open Data MF SR (opendata.mfsr.sk)
why_relevant: Machine-readable ministry datasets (budget, public-administration reporting) enabling structured tracking of state-entity finances without PDF parsing.

source_name: MF SR – Výkazníctvo subjektov verejnej správy (FIN 1-12 až FIN 6-04)
why_relevant: Defines the statutory reporting obligations, forms and deadlines for public-administration entities — the rulebook that tells a collector what documents must exist, in what format, and when.

source_name: FinStat.sk – entity financial profiles (SZRB, EXIMBANKA, SIH, MH Invest)
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator normalising filed statements into time series per IČO; fastest way to build comparable multi-year profit/asset trends across the state-owned financial perimeter, and to detect a newly filed report.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (orsr.sk) – corporate extracts of state financial entities
why_relevant: Authoritative legal identity, historical name changes (e.g. SZRB Asset Management → Slovak Investment Holding), statutory bodies and ownership; needed to keep the actor map correct across renames.

source_name: Úrad vlády SR – tlačové správy (government press office)
why_relevant: Government-level announcements on financial-sector credibility, state bank capitalisations and mandates; gives the political framing and timing around state-entity reporting.

source_name: Wikipedia (EN) – Slovak Guarantee and Development Bank
why_relevant: English-language entry point that fixes the official English name and history of SZRB; useful for cross-language query construction, not as a factual source.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Referencie (customer references)
why_relevant: ACE is the dominant local core-banking / building-savings / omnichannel vendor for SK banks; its own reference page names bank customers, which is often the only public record of a private bank's core system supplier.

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Správy / press releases (SK newsroom)
why_relevant: Vendor press releases announce SK bank wins and go-lives (e.g. 30-years-partner-of-banks piece referencing Poštová banka, 365.bank, Slovenská sporiteľňa card processing).

source_name: Asseco Central Europe — Výročné správy (annual reports, PDF archive)
why_relevant: Annual reports carry segment revenue by banking/finance vertical, named large contracts and backlog commentary — the closest thing to disclosed spend by private SK banks on core systems.

source_name: Registeruz.sk — statutory financial statements & annual reports of vendor legal entities (e.g. Asseco Central Europe a.s., IČO 35760419)
why_relevant: Slovak register of financial statements holds filed accounts/annual reports for every SK-registered vendor subsidiary (Asseco CE, Printec Slovakia, Diebold Nixdorf s.r.o., NCR/Atleos entities), enabling revenue sizing of SK banking-tech spend where vendor group reports do not break out SK.
